main_text.p: distinctionem ab Aristotele categoriis præmissam,& tàtopere in omni disquisitione necessariam,( unde vel in primis utra pars de cœna Domini disceptantium sophisticè ageret, poterat cognosci) neglexisse, altóq; præteriisse silentio? Inde enim, quòd sunt aliqua quæ tam intra quàm extra orationis complexum, nomē unà cum re, aliqua sine re solum nomen cōmune habent, nullo negotio deprehenditur, cùm panis mysticus tum τῷ σύμ-πλοκῷ, tum αὐτὸ συμπλοκῆς, Christi corpus dicatur: nec tamen sub eandē corporis Christi definitionem cadat: quòd corporis Christi nomen pani neutrobi συνωνύμως, sed aut ὁμωνύ-μως, aut alia quapiam ratione tribuatur. Ergo valeat ea ratio quam Cyprianus & Augustinus è sacramentalibus sanctæ scripturæ locutionibus observatam, pro regula nobis reliquerunt: nempe, quòd in divinis mysteriis & sacramentis, res sensibiles & significantes, pro similitudine, non ipsa rerum veritate si-

page.notes: The Greek words are set in italic type. The Greek on the fourth-to-last line, "τῷ σύμ-πλοκῷ" and "αὐτὸ συμπλοκῆς", is hard to read at this resolution. The first letters of the Greek were read with some doubt and should be checked against a higher-resolution scan. The Greek "συνωνύμως" and "ὁμωνύμως" are split across the line end as printed. The page is a continuation, so the opening paragraph carries cont="true". The text ends on the hyphenated fragment "si-" as printed. The left strip of the scan shows the neighbouring page's edge and show-through, which is not transcribed.
